description.firstVisit: The campus is already in motion when you arrive on Monday morning. Students cross the central plaza with coffee cups and half-open backpacks; a shuttle pulls away from the curb while bicycles rattle against the racks. The notice board stands beside the main walkway, with the lecture hall, library and café all within a short walk. Mira is checking the announcements nearby. The day is beginning, but you are free to decide how to spend the morning.
description.returnVisit: The central plaza stays busy as students move between classes. The notice board carries updated lecture announcements, club activities and a few notices from the East District. The library and café remain easy places to step away from the crowd.

actions.label: Check today's campus notices
actions.feedback: The board lists a 09:00 introductory Research Methods lecture in the Lecture Hall, club activities at the Student Union and several volunteer notices. A neighborhood post from the East District catches your eye, but nothing requires you to follow it.

description.firstVisit: Rows of tiered seats face a wide projection screen. Students compare notes while the lecturer arranges the morning's Research Methods slides. A few seats near the aisle are still free, and the room gradually fills as the 09:00 lecture approaches.
description.returnVisit: The lecture hall empties between classes. The projector hums softly while students pack their laptops and compare notes before heading to the next building.

actions.label: Attend the lecture
actions.feedback: The lecturer introduces basic research methods: trace a claim to its source, distinguish firsthand observations from hearsay and compare accounts for contradictions. You take notes and leave with a clearer plan for your coursework.

description.firstVisit: The library is quiet without feeling empty. Long shared desks sit beneath warm lights, reference shelves line the back wall and a printer rattles near the front desk. Sera has settled at a window-side desk with her coursework spread out. It is a good place to prepare before the morning lecture.
description.returnVisit: The library remains a refuge from the noise outside. Students work at the shared desks, Sera often studies near the windows and the printer occasionally interrupts the silence.

actions.label: Find a place to study
actions.feedback: You find a quiet desk, review the course outline and mark a few questions to follow up during the morning lecture.

description.firstVisit: The campus café smells of espresso and toasted bread. A short queue forms near the counter while students claim tables between classes. By late morning, familiar groups gather near the windows to compare notes and make plans for the rest of the day.
description.returnVisit: The café grows busier toward lunchtime. The queue shifts slowly, and familiar groups occupy their usual tables while students trade updates between classes.

actions.label: Get something to eat
actions.feedback: You finish a warm meal. Your energy returns and the noise of the café feels a little less overwhelming.

actions.label: Chat with other students
actions.feedback: You exchange a few stories with other students about the morning lecture, upcoming deadlines and which campus activities are worth checking out.

events.title: A Seat at the Table
events.description: A few students at the window table are discussing a strange post from the East District community board. One of them recognizes you and makes room. The conversation is casual, but the details do not quite add up.

choices.label: Join the conversation
choices.feedback: You join in. The post describes a vacant apartment where someone hears a child crying at the same time every night. One of the students says the address is in the East District.

choices.label: Take your food and find a quiet seat
choices.feedback: You leave the conversation alone and enjoy a quiet meal.

description.firstVisit: Your apartment is small but comfortable: a bed, a desk crowded with notebooks, a kitchenette and a window facing the neighboring buildings. Your laptop is still open where you left it last night. It is not much space, but it is yours.
description.returnVisit: Your apartment is quiet and familiar. The desk is waiting for your coursework and the bed is an easy place to disappear for a while.

actions.label: Check the mail by the door
actions.feedback: There is a utility bill and a flyer for a neighborhood event. Nothing urgent.

description.firstVisit: The East District is a mix of apartment blocks, small shops and narrow side streets. Delivery riders weave through traffic while residents stop at convenience stores on their way home. Community notices and local business ads cover the glass panels at the bus stop.
description.returnVisit: Traffic moves through the district while shopkeepers prepare for the evening rush. The apartment block is a short walk from the main road.

actions.label: Browse the neighborhood forum
actions.feedback: Several posts mention Unit 213 in the old apartment block. The reports disagree, but multiple people describe hearing a child crying at 2:13 a.m.

description.firstVisit: A narrow café sits between a laundromat and a convenience store. The counter is crowded with takeaway cups, and a handwritten shift roster is pinned beside the staff entrance. It is a familiar place for students looking for a part-time job.
description.returnVisit: The café is busy with its usual mix of regulars, delivery orders and students taking a break from work or study.

actions.label: Work a café shift
actions.feedback: You finish your shift, wipe down the counter and collect your pay. It is tiring, but the extra money helps.

description.firstVisit: The apartment block stands behind a row of shuttered shops. Several windows are boarded up, and the entry intercom has a handwritten note saying the building is awaiting renovation. The lobby smells of damp concrete. A stairwell light flickers above the directory; Unit 213 is still listed, though the name beside it has been scratched away.
description.returnVisit: The old apartment block is as quiet as before. The entry light flickers and the directory still lists Unit 213 without a resident's name.

actions.label: Read the renovation notice
actions.feedback: The notice says the upper floors have been closed for months. Unit 213 is not listed among the apartments cleared for renovation.

events.title: The 2:13 AM Incident
events.description: A faint child's sob comes from somewhere above you. It stops as soon as you reach the second-floor landing. A moment later, three soft knocks come from behind the door marked 213. Your phone shows 2:13 a.m. in an old forum screenshot, but it is not that late now. The building is otherwise silent.

choices.label: Stay in the hallway and listen
choices.feedback: The crying returns in short bursts, each separated by the same interval. You notice that the sound seems to come from inside the bedroom, not the hallway.

choices.label: Open the door to Unit 213
choices.feedback: The door gives way with a dry click. Inside, a child's voice repeats the same unfinished sentence. When you step toward the bedroom, it calls your name. You back out before it can come closer.

choices.label: Leave the building
choices.feedback: You decide not to take the risk. The street noise feels unusually comforting after the silence inside.

description.firstVisit: A modest office occupies the second floor above a repair shop. The reception area has a few chairs, a stack of incident forms and a notice explaining that the company assesses unusual reports before accepting a case. Nothing about the place looks mysterious; it feels like an ordinary service business.
description.returnVisit: The office is open during business hours. A small sign directs visitors to the reception desk.

description.firstVisit: The student union is full of club posters, event sign-ups and groups planning their next activity. A few students are rehearsing a presentation near the windows while someone tries to recruit passers-by for a weekend trip.
description.returnVisit: Club members come and go throughout the day. New posters appear beside the familiar announcements.

actions.label: Ask about student clubs
actions.feedback: You speak with a few club members and take a flyer for an upcoming campus event.

actions.label: Look through the volunteer board
actions.feedback: Most listings are routine errands and event staffing. You leave the board feeling that none of them is quite what you are looking for.

description.firstVisit: The sports field sits behind the gym. A few students run laps while others practice passing drills near the equipment shed. Noah is finishing his morning training before heading to class. The noise of the central campus feels far away here.
description.returnVisit: Students use the field for short practice sessions throughout the day. The equipment shed is open, and the track remains busy between classes.

actions.label: Practice for a while
actions.feedback: You repeat a few basic drills, take a short water break and finish feeling more familiar with the movements.

description.firstVisit: The campus clinic is clean and practical. A receptionist checks appointments while a nurse organizes supplies behind the counter. The place is quiet apart from the printer and the occasional phone call.
description.returnVisit: The clinic continues to handle routine appointments and minor injuries.

actions.label: Receive treatment
actions.feedback: You rest while the clinic staff tend to your injuries.

description.firstVisit: A paved path follows the river past a row of trees and outdoor exercise equipment. Joggers pass in both directions, and a few people sit on the low wall watching the water. It is a good place to clear your head.
description.returnVisit: The river keeps moving past the park. Joggers and students drift along the path as the light changes.

actions.label: Take a quiet break
actions.feedback: You sit by the river for a while. The noise of the city fades into the background.
